findings.evidence: The statement claims the connecting map is an isomorphism for every n>0, but line 57 deduces L_{n-1}^PF(Q)=0 from positive-degree vanishing. For n=1 that term is L_0^PF(Q)\cong F(Q), which need not vanish, so the claimed isomorphism fails in general.

The statement claims the connecting map is an isomorphism for every n>0, but line 57 deduces R_I^{n-1}F(J)=0 from positive-degree vanishing. For n=1 that term is R_I^0F(J)\cong F(J), which need not vanish, so the claimed isomorphism fails in general.

Fact L3 cites ex-the-cone-long-exact-sequence-for-multiplication-by-m as the witness for a nonzero connecting morphism, but that cited example only computes the middle multiplication-by-m map in a cone long exact sequence and does not exhibit a nonzero connecting morphism. The nearby published item ex-a-degreewise-split-sequence-with-nonzero-connecting-map does.
